# @zakkster/lite-sketch

Version: 1.1.2
License: MIT (c) Zahary Shinikchiev <shinikchiev@yahoo.com>
Runtime dependencies: none. ESM only. ASCII-only source. sideEffects: false.
Node: >= 18.

## What it is

A zero-dependency, zero-GC family of APPROXIMATE streaming summaries (sketches)
that WITNESSES its ACCURACY instead of only citing it: every member proves its
MEASURED error against the paper's THEORETICAL bound, next to the memory it saves.
It is the approximate-aggregate corner of the suite -- @zakkster/lite-filter is
approximate MEMBERSHIP, @zakkster/lite-o1 is EXACT O(1), and lite-sketch is
APPROXIMATE aggregates (count / frequency / quantile / top-k).

v1.1.2 ships the STABLE FOUR-member API -- the complete roster: HyperLogLog (distinct-count /
cardinality), CountMinSketch (point-query frequency), and SpaceSaving (heavy hitters
/ top-k) over the shipped, avalanche-tested two-lane 64-bit hash, plus DDSketch
(relative-error quantiles), which bins raw values on a log scale and does NOT use the
hash. 1.0.0 froze this four-member surface stable (semver). 1.1.0 is post-1.0 hardening:
ADDITIVE new API -- DDSketch's `addFrom(buf, i)` zero-box entry point + the
strict/minIndexable/maxIndexable/rangeMin/rangeMax getters -- plus fail-closed fixes
(HLL/CMS reject non-integer / +-Infinity keys). No API removed; backward compatible.
Members share no mutable module state, so a bundler that imports one drops the others
(tree-shakeable). One member per question: distinct-count, frequency, quantiles, top-k.

## Exports (from the single main file Sketch.js)

- `HyperLogLog` -- class. A zero-GC distinct-count (cardinality) sketch over a dense
  `Uint8Array(m)` of one-byte registers, `m = 2^p`, `p in [4, 18]`. `add(key)` is
  worst-case O(1), 0 B/op (hash the key over the two-lane mix, pick a register by the
  top p bits, record `rho` = leftmost-1 of the remaining 64-p bits as a running max).
  `addHashed(hi, lo)` is the pre-hashed fast path. `count()` is a cold O(m) estimator
  (Ertl's improved estimator, 2017 -- a single table-free formula accurate across the
  whole range, no empirical bias tables), a disclosed co-headline, NOT per-add. `merge(other)` is register-wise max (equal-m-or-throw); `clear()` reuses
  the allocation. Standard error `1.04/sqrt(m)` (statistical, two-sided). Dense-only
  (sparse deferred); no crypto hashing. Fail closed on a bad p (throws typeof-first
  BEFORE allocation); `add` guards a non-number key; `count` / getters never throw.
- `CountMinSketch` -- class. A zero-GC point-query FREQUENCY sketch over a dense
  `Uint32Array(d * w)` counter matrix (d rows x w columns, w a power of two). `add(key,
  count = 1)` / `addHashed(hi, lo, count = 1)` are worst-case O(d), 0 B/op (one increment
  per row); `estimate(key)` / `estimateHashed(hi, lo)` return the MIN of the d cells -- the
  one-sided over-estimate while `!saturated` (`f_hat >= f_true`, `f_hat - f_true <= epsilon*N`
  w.p. `1 - delta`, `epsilon = e/w`, `delta = e^-d`; once a counter saturates at 2^32-1 the
  sticky `saturated` getter is set and a query over a saturated key may read low). Conservative update (Estan-Varghese) is the DEFAULT
  (tightens the over-estimate on skewed streams); `conservative: false` is the classic
  linearly-mergeable plain matrix. `CountMinSketch.withAccuracy(epsilon, delta)` sizes it from
  the paper's bound (and THROWS when the request is unattainable -- w > 2^25 or d > 32 -- not
  clamp). `merge(other)` is element-wise saturating add (equal-d/w/seed-or-throw; a
  cross-`conservative` merge is allowed, `this` keeps its flag, and `saturated` is carried);
  `clear()` reuses the allocation and resets `saturated`. Counters saturate at 2^32-1. Fail
  closed on a bad ctor arg / key / lane / count, a count > 2^32-1, or a running total past
  2^53-1 (throws typeof-first BEFORE allocation); `estimate` never throws (a key `add` would
  reject estimates 0, never aliasing a real key).
- `DDSketch` -- class. A zero-GC relative-error QUANTILE sketch over a dense
  `Float64Array` of log-scale bins (`gamma = (1+alpha)/(1-alpha)`; a value x>0 lands in
  bucket `ceil(ln(x)/ln(gamma))`). `add(value, count = 1)` is worst-case O(1), 0 B/op;
  `quantile(q)` is a cold O(bins) cumulative walk returning a value within a HARD relative
  error `|v - v_true| <= alpha * v_true` (the family's sharpest guarantee -- per-query, not
  statistical). Collapsing-lowest by default (bounded memory, tail-accurate p50/p90/p99);
  a `{ range: [min, max] }` option is strict fixed-range fail-closed. Positive + zero domain
  (a negative value throws). `merge(other)` is same-alpha-or-throw; `min`/`max` are EXACT
  (not bucketed). Fail closed on a bad alpha / value / out-of-indexable-range / count (throws
  typeof-first BEFORE allocation); `quantile` / getters never throw (a bad q -> NaN). Does
  NOT use the two-lane hash.
- `DD_ALPHA_MIN` -- number, 1e-6. The smallest `alpha` the `DDSketch` ctor accepts
  (`DD_ALPHA_MIN <= alpha < 1`); a smaller alpha throws [lite-sketch] at the ctor door.
- `SpaceSaving` -- class. A zero-GC HEAVY-HITTERS / TOP-K sketch (Metwally et al.) over a
  fixed `capacity` (k) counters: an intrusive frequency-bucket forest (O(1) increment + find-min)
  plus a fixed open-addressing key map, over the two-lane hash. `add(key, count = 1)` is
  amortized O(1), 0 B/op -- increment a monitored key, insert a free slot, or (when full) EVICT
  the min-count key and reassign its slot at `count = min + count`, `error = min` (eviction IS the
  algorithm; it NEVER fails at capacity). Guarantee: every key with true freq > N/k is monitored
  (NO false negatives); a monitored key's true count is in `[count - error, count]`; error <= N/k.
  `estimate(key)` / `errorOf(key)` are O(1) (0 if not monitored); `topK(n)` / `heavyHitters(threshold)`
  return sorted entries (COLD, ALLOCATE); `forEach` is alloc-free; `merge(other)` (same-capacity/seed)
  keeps the top-k. `SpaceSaving.withError(epsilon)` sizes k = ceil(1/epsilon). There is deliberately
  NO addHashed (it stores key identities, so there is no honest pre-hashed path). Fail closed on a
  bad ctor arg / key / count (typeof-first, byte-identical no-op); queries never throw.
- `VERSION` -- string, '1.1.2'.

(The canonical hash is used internally by HyperLogLog / CountMinSketch `add`; a caller who
brings their own good hash uses `addHashed(hi, lo)`. DDSketch bins raw values -- no hash.
ADR 0001 records the hash.)

## HyperLogLog

    new HyperLogLog(p = 14, seed = <default uint32>)

- p: precision; integer in [4, 18]. Register count m = 2^p; memory = m bytes
  (p=14 -> 16 KB). Standard error = 1.04/sqrt(m) (p=14 -> ~0.8%). Higher p halves
  the error each +2 and quadruples the memory.
- seed: per-instance uint32 (default a fixed constant), coerced via >>> 0; a bad
  seed throws [lite-sketch] typeof-first.
- Constructor throws [lite-sketch] on a non-integer / out-of-range p BEFORE the
  Uint8Array is allocated (nothing half-built escapes).

Hot surface (add / addHashed are worst-case O(1), zero allocation):

- add(key) -> this          Hash a SAFE-INTEGER key (|key| <= 2^53 - 1) over the two-lane
                            mix and record its register (running max of rho). The hot body
                            distinguishes low word + high word + sign, so the whole safe-integer
                            range is accepted (matching CountMinSketch / SpaceSaving). Fail
                            closed: a non-number / NaN / Symbol / BigInt / +-Infinity /
                            non-integer / out-of-safe-range key throws [lite-sketch]
                            (typeof-first, byte-identical no-op) -- a non-integer or Infinity
                            would truncate/alias under the 32-bit word split.
- addHashed(hi, lo) -> this  The PRE-HASHED fast path: two uint32 lanes the caller
                            hashed with their own good hash; skips the internal mix.
                            Both lanes typeof-guarded as uint32.
- count() -> number         COLD, O(m): the estimated distinct count via Ertl's IMPROVED
                            estimator (2017) -- a single TABLE-FREE formula
                            (`alpha_inf * m^2 / z`, `alpha_inf = 1/(2 ln 2)`; z folds the
                            register multiplicity vector through the self-terminating
                            sigma/tau corrections) accurate across the WHOLE range: no
                            range-switching, no HLL++ empirical bias tables. A disclosed
                            co-headline (the O(m) scan), NOT a per-add cost. Never throws.
- merge(other) -> this      Register-wise max of `other` into `this` (the union).
                            Throws [lite-sketch] on a non-HyperLogLog or unequal m
                            (equal-m-or-throw, the same-capacity discipline).
- clear() -> this           Zero the registers; reuse the same allocation.
- p (getter)                The precision p.
- m (getter)                Register count, 2^p.
- standardError (getter)    1.04 / sqrt(m) -- the theoretical relative standard error.

Accuracy contract (the honesty anchor): the witness drives HLL on a stream with an
exact Set oracle, measures the relative error, and GATES it against theory -- RMS
relative error <= ~1.5 * 1.04/sqrt(m) over an N-sweep, p99 within ~3 sigma, error
halving as p += 2. The exact-Set foil's memory grows O(distinct) while HLL stays a
fixed m bytes (the space co-headline). Uniformity is STATISTICAL, not cryptographic.

## CountMinSketch

    new CountMinSketch(d, w, options?)
    CountMinSketch.withAccuracy(epsilon, delta, options?) -> CountMinSketch

- d: depth (hash rows); integer in [1, 32]. w: width (columns/row); integer in
  [1, 2^25], ROUNDED UP to a power of two. A hard d*w <= 2^31 cap keeps every flat
  counter index a SMI. Memory = d * w * 4 bytes.
- options (object): { seed = <default uint32> (coerced |0), conservative = true }. An
  unknown option key throws [lite-sketch] with a did-you-mean hint.
- withAccuracy inverts the bound: w = ceil(e/epsilon) (rounded up to a power of two),
  d = ceil(ln(1/delta)) (clamped UP to >= 1); epsilon in (0,1), delta in (0,1). An
  UNATTAINABLE request -- w > 2^25 or d > 32 -- THROWS [lite-sketch], it does not clamp
  down to a weaker guarantee. The achieved epsilon (= e/w) and delta (= e^-d) read back via getters.
- Constructor throws [lite-sketch] typeof-first on a bad d / w / seed / conservative /
  unknown option BEFORE the Uint32Array is allocated (nothing half-built escapes).

Hot surface (add / addHashed / estimate are worst-case O(d), zero allocation):

- add(key, count = 1) -> this     Hash a SAFE-INTEGER key (|key| <= 2^53 - 1) + increment one
                                  cell per row (the min-query answer is a one-sided over-estimate).
                                  The hot body distinguishes low word + high word + sign, so the
                                  whole safe-integer range is accepted (matching HyperLogLog /
                                  SpaceSaving). count is a positive integer in [1, 2^32-1];
                                  counters SATURATE at 2^32-1 (never wrap) and set the sticky
                                  `saturated` getter (one-sided only while !saturated). Fail
                                  closed: a non-number / NaN / +-Infinity / non-integer /
                                  out-of-safe-range key, a count outside [1, 2^32-1], or an add
                                  that would push the running total past 2^53-1 throws
                                  [lite-sketch] (typeof-first) -- a non-integer or Infinity would
                                  truncate/alias under the 32-bit word split.
- addHashed(hi, lo, count = 1) -> this  The PRE-HASHED fast path: two uint32 lanes the caller
                                  hashed; skips the internal mix. Both lanes typeof-guarded uint32.
- estimate(key) -> number         The estimated frequency: the MIN of the key's d cells. QUERY,
                                  NEVER throws -- a key `add` would reject (non-integer / non-finite
                                  / out-of-safe-range) returns 0 and never aliases a real key.
- estimateHashed(hi, lo) -> number  Query form of the pre-hashed path; a non-uint32 lane returns 0.
- merge(other) -> this            Element-wise SATURATING ADD of other into this. Throws
                                  [lite-sketch] on a non-CountMinSketch, mismatched d / w / seed, or
                                  a running total past 2^53-1. EXACT for plain (conservative:false)
                                  sketches; a valid but looser upper bound for conservative ones; a
                                  cross-`conservative` merge is allowed (this keeps its own flag),
                                  and `saturated` is carried from either side.
- clear() -> this                 Zero the counters, the running total, and `saturated`; reuse the allocation.
- d / w / seed / conservative     Getters (the frozen shape + mode).
- total (getter)                  The exact running sum N of all added counts.
- saturated (getter)              Sticky: true once any counter clamped at 2^32-1 (one-sided only
                                  while false); carried by merge, reset by clear().
- epsilon (getter)                e / w -- the theoretical additive-error fraction.
- delta (getter)                  e^-d -- the theoretical failure probability.

Conservative update (default, Estan-Varghese): raise the d cells only to min(cells) + count
instead of +count on every row -- never changes the min-query answer, provably tightens the
over-estimate on skewed (Zipfian) streams. It is NOT linearly mergeable, so plain mode
(conservative:false) is the choice when distributing then merging (plain merge is exact).

Accuracy contract (the honesty anchor): the witness drives a Zipfian stream against an exact
Map oracle, measures the over-estimate per key, and GATES the fraction exceeding epsilon*N at
<= delta, plus one-sidedness (0 undercounts) and conservative <= plain. Space co-headline:
d*w*4 bytes vs the exact Map's O(distinct) footprint. The over-estimate is ONE-SIDED (never
under) WHILE `!saturated` -- once a counter clamps at 2^32-1 the sticky `saturated` getter is
set and that key may read low; the guarantee is probabilistic (delta), the hashing statistical not cryptographic.

## DDSketch

    new DDSketch(alpha, options?)

- alpha: relative accuracy, in [1e-6, 1) -- the guarantee knob (e.g. 0.01 = 1% relative error).
  The floor is the exported DD_ALPHA_MIN (1e-6); a smaller alpha throws [lite-sketch] at the ctor
  door (at the 2^20-bin cap it spans only ~8x of value range, and smaller alphas once hung the
  bound search for seconds). gamma = (1+alpha)/(1-alpha); a value x>0 lands in bucket
  key(x) = ceil(ln(x)/ln(gamma)), and the representative 2*gamma^key/(gamma+1) is within alpha
  relative error of every x in the bucket.
- options (object): { maxBins = 2048, range?: [min, max] }. An unknown option key throws
  [lite-sketch] (did-you-mean).
  - DEFAULT (no range) = COLLAPSING-LOWEST: a dense Float64Array(maxBins); when the value range
    exceeds the budget, the SMALLEST-value buckets collapse into the floor bin. Unbounded value
    range, bounded memory; the relative-error guarantee is PRESERVED for the UPPER quantiles
    (p50/p90/p99) and degraded only for the smallest values (a disclosed co-headline). `collapsed`
    getter reports whether any collapse has happened.
  - range present = STRICT fixed-range fail-closed: bins cover exactly [key(min), key(max)]; a value
    with x>0 whose key is outside the range THROWS [lite-sketch] (never collapsed). Requires 0 < min < max.
- DOMAIN = positive + zero: x>0 is bucketed, x===0 increments a separate zero counter, x<0 THROWS
  [lite-sketch] (no negative mirror; deferred). Values outside the indexable double range (roughly
  (~2.2e-308, ~8.9e307] at alpha=0.01, low end EXCLUSIVE; the window widens as alpha grows) THROW
  fail-closed so the bucket representative can never overflow to Infinity or underflow to 0. The
  EXACT runtime bounds are the minIndexable / maxIndexable getters -- the exact acceptance edges of
  add's own key expression (bit-level bisected in the ctor), not an off-by-ulps pow(gamma, K+-1).
- Constructor throws [lite-sketch] typeof-first on a bad alpha / maxBins / range BEFORE allocation.

Hot surface (add is worst-case O(1), zero allocation):

- add(value, count = 1) -> this    Bucket a finite value (or increment the zero counter). count is a
                                  positive integer in [1, 2^32-1]. Fail closed: a non-number / NaN /
                                  +-Infinity / negative / out-of-indexable-range value, a count outside
                                  [1, 2^32-1], or an add that would push the running count past 2^53-1
                                  throws [lite-sketch] (typeof-first, BYTE-IDENTICAL no-op -- no
                                  aggregate is touched on a rejected add; the count check runs before
                                  the negative-value check, so a doubly-invalid add names the count,
                                  but a non-finite value is still caught first, so add(NaN, 2^32) names
                                  the value).
- addFrom(buf, i) -> this          Add buf[i] (count = 1), the ZERO-BOX entry point for a FRACTIONAL
                                  hot-path value: add(fractionalDouble) boxes its tagged argument (~16 B
                                  HeapNumber/call) when V8 does not inline the call; addFrom reads buf[i]
                                  from a caller-owned Float64Array UNBOXED, so a fractional value stays
                                  0 B/op. Same validation / throws / binning as add. Fail closed on a
                                  non-Float64Array buf, an out-of-bounds / non-integer i, or a value add
                                  would reject. Use it for a computed fractional value (e.g. a span
                                  duration): write it into a length-1 scratch, then addFrom(scratch, 0).
- quantile(q) -> number           The q-quantile (q in [0,1]) within alpha relative error. COLD,
                                  O(bins) cumulative walk; rank = floor(q*(count-1)); returns the
                                  bucket representative (or 0 if the rank falls in the zero bucket).
                                  NEVER throws -- an empty sketch or a bad q returns NaN.
- merge(other) -> this            Fold other's bins/zeroCount/count/sum into this (collapsing as
                                  needed), carrying other.collapsed forward (collapsed mass makes this
                                  collapsed). Same-alpha (same gamma)-or-throw; a strict `this` throws if
                                  an incoming key is out of range OR if `other` is collapsed (its low-end
                                  mass has already folded). min/max combined exactly. O(other bins).
- clear() -> this                 Zero the bins + all scalars; reuse the allocation.
- alpha / count / sum             Getters: the accuracy knob; the exact element count N; the exact sum.
- min / max                       Getters: the EXACT tracked min / max (NOT bucketed -- exact while
                                  quantile is alpha-approximate); NaN on an empty sketch.
- zeroCount / maxBins / numBins   Getters: the exact count of zeros; the bin capacity; the live
                                  (populated) bin count.
- collapsed (getter)              Whether any smallest-value collapse has occurred (the small-value
                                  guarantee was touched).
- strict (getter)                 Whether this is a STRICT fixed-range sketch (a range was given).
- minIndexable / maxIndexable     Getters: the EXACT x bounds add() accepts at this alpha, the
                                  bit-level bisected edges of add's own key expression -- add accepts
                                  finite minIndexable < x <= maxIndexable (plus exact 0). minIndexable is
                                  the exclusive low floor (~2.2e-308 at alpha=0.01); maxIndexable is the
                                  inclusive ceiling (~8.9e307 at alpha=0.01, always below Number.MAX_VALUE).
- rangeMin / rangeMax             Getters: STRICT mode -- the configured range ends (NaN if not strict).

Accuracy contract (the honesty anchor -- the family's sharpest): the guarantee is a HARD PER-QUERY
relative-error bound |v_returned - v_true| <= alpha * v_true, not a statistical (HLL) or additive (CMS)
one. The witness drives uniform + lognormal + pareto positive streams against an exact sorted-array
oracle and GATES the measured relative error at q in {0.5, 0.9, 0.99, 0.999} against alpha. Space
co-headline: maxBins*8 bytes (fixed) vs the exact sorted array's 8*N bytes. Uniformity is not a factor
(no hashing); the only approximation is the log-bucket width, bounded by alpha.

## SpaceSaving

    new SpaceSaving(capacity, options?)
    SpaceSaving.withError(epsilon, options?) -> SpaceSaving

- capacity: k, the number of monitored counters; integer in [1, 2^24]. options { seed = <default
  uint32> }; an unknown option key throws [lite-sketch] (did-you-mean). Memory is fixed at k counters.
- withError inverts the guarantee: k = ceil(1/epsilon), epsilon in (0,1); an UNATTAINABLE request
  (k > 2^24) THROWS [lite-sketch], it does not clamp down. The achieved epsilon (= 1/k) reads back via a getter.
- Constructor throws [lite-sketch] typeof-first on a bad capacity / seed / option BEFORE allocation.

The algorithm: monitor k (key -> count, error) triples. add(key): if monitored -> increment; if a slot
is free (< k tracked) -> insert (count, error 0); if FULL -> EVICT the MIN-count monitored key, reassign
its slot to the newcomer at count = min + count and error = min (the evicted count is the newcomer's max
over-count). It NEVER fails at capacity -- eviction IS the algorithm. Guarantee: every element with true
frequency > N/k is monitored (NO false negatives); a monitored key's true count lies in [count - error,
count]; error <= the current min counter <= N/k.

Hot surface (add is amortized O(1), zero allocation):

- add(key, count = 1) -> this      Add a SAFE-INTEGER key (|key| <= 2^53; 0 is legal) with a positive
                                  integer count in [1, 2^32-1]. Increment / insert / evict-min per the
                                  state. Fail closed: a non-safe-integer key, a count outside
                                  [1, 2^32-1], or an add that would push the running total past 2^53-1
                                  throws [lite-sketch] (typeof-first, BYTE-IDENTICAL no-op).
                                  (There is NO addHashed -- SpaceSaving stores key identities.)
- estimate(key) -> number         The estimated frequency (an upper bound), or 0 if not monitored. O(1),
                                  never throws.
- errorOf(key) -> number          The over-estimate bound (true count in [estimate - errorOf, estimate]),
                                  or 0 if not monitored. O(1), never throws.
- forEach(fn) -> void             Alloc-free walk of monitored entries (storage order, NOT sorted):
                                  fn(key, count, error, ss).
- topK(n = size) -> Array<{key,count,error}>   The top n by count, DESC. COLD, ALLOCATES. Never throws.
- heavyHitters(threshold) -> Array<{key,count,error}>   Every monitored key with count > threshold*total
                                  -- a SUPERSET with NO false negatives (may include false positives);
                                  filter by (count - error) > threshold*total for the guaranteed subset.
                                  COLD, ALLOCATES. Never throws.
- merge(other) -> this            Union two summaries (min-imputation for absent keys), keep the top-k.
                                  Throws [lite-sketch] on a non-SpaceSaving or unequal capacity/seed;
                                  the bracket guarantee survives (looser). O(k), a bounded cold scratch.
- clear() -> this                 Drop all monitored keys; reuse the pools.
- capacity / size / total         Getters: k; the monitored count (<= k); the exact running sum N.
- epsilon (getter)                1 / capacity -- the theoretical error fraction.
- seed (getter)                   The uint32 hash seed.

Accuracy contract (the honesty anchor): the witness drives a Zipfian stream against an exact Map oracle
and GATES that recall of the true hitters above N/k is 100% (NO false negatives), the bracket
count - error <= true <= count holds for every monitored key, and error <= N/k. Space co-headline: k
counters (fixed) vs the exact Map's O(distinct). The over-estimate is one-sided (never undercounts a
monitored key); uniformity is statistical (the hash), not cryptographic.

## The hash (ADR 0001)

A shipped two-lane 64-bit-quality non-crypto mix (Math.imul finalizer, murmur3 /
xxh32 style), realized as two uint32 lanes returned through module-scope slots (NO
BigInt -- it allocates), so the hot path is 0 B/op. HLL reads BOTH lanes for rho
(a single 32-bit hash would cap rho at 32-p bits and lose large-cardinality
accuracy). A pre-hashed fast path (addHashed); seeded row-salting for future
multi-row members (h_i = mix(h ^ i*ODD_CONST), per-instance seed); an optional
alloc-free string-bytes hasher. Avalanche-tested: a 1-bit input flip flips ~half
the output bits across both lanes.

## Scripts

- npm test          -- node:test behavioral + fail-closed suites + the hash avalanche test
- npm run witness   -- the accuracy witness (measured error vs the theoretical bound)
- npm run torture   -- the 0 B/op leak + GC-profiler gate on add (node --expose-gc)
- npm run test:perf -- flat-throughput perf gate + a must-allocate control
- npm run lanes     -- child-process scavenge/deopt lanes (HLL add <= 2, N5 deopts <= 3, teeth control)
- npm run verify    -- test + test:types + torture + witness + test:perf + lanes (the release gate)

## Roadmap

HyperLogLog (0.1.0, cardinality) -> CountMinSketch (0.2.0, frequency) -> DDSketch
(0.3.0, quantiles, HARD relative-error bound) -> SpaceSaving (0.4.0, heavy hitters)
-> 1.0.0 (API declared stable at four members). Post-1.0: KMV/MinHash, CountSketch,
HeavyKeeper, SlidingHLL -- one per release.
